answer: Recurring proof-of-personhood gatherings are one concrete sybil guard. At each summit, small groups sign each other's keys, so one human backs one key per round. Weight comes only after several summits, forming a steady river of independent attestations; the network reads this history as its signal, not a declared profile. A sybil cannot mint membership at home: each fake needs a distinct human present, repeatedly. Bribes scale linearly, and once a forged group is exposed its branch is revoked, so more identities mean more loss, not influence.
